mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate below 2.0% over the prior month compresses discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate accommodative monetary policy.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS declines below 2.0% for at least 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 5.5% for two consecutive months, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce corporate profit expectations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 5.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1050.0 and retail sales (RSAFS) below 380000.0 for two consecutive months indicates weakening consumer demand, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where both HOUST and RSAFS decline below their thresholds for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 110.0 for two consecutive months signals manufacturing slowdown, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced corporate output expectations.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances during late-cycle expansions when INDPRO falls below 110.0.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) above 1070.0 for two consecutive months indicates robust consumer spending, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days through elevated retail sales and corporate revenue growth.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where HOUST exceeds 1070.0 for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When year-over-year CPI exceeds 3.0%, it signals persistent inflation that triggers aggressive monetary tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to rising discount rates.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL YoY exceeds 3.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in payrolls (PAYEMS) above 137500.0 and decrease in unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5.6% for two consecutive months indicates labor market strength that boosts consumer spending, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where both PAYEMS exceeds 137500.0 and UNRATE falls below 5.6% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: In recessionary conditions, a rebound in real GDP growth (GDPC1) above 0.5% quarterly rate triggers positive equity returns as the market prices in economic recovery over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances during recessionary conditions when GDPC1 rebounds above 0.5% QoQ.
